rows.value_as_printed: No sample cooling/heating control on MM 400; cooling only by manual LN2 pre-cooling of the steel jar
rows.quote: For applications which require cooling or heating the sample, the Mixer Mill MM 500 control is the perfect choice.
rows.document_title: Laboratory Mixer Mill MM 400 - RETSCH (product page)
rows.location: Product description, intro paragraphs (cached research/v5/cache/c7591d067d40187a.txt line 305); see also CryoKit section line 447: 'Indirect embrittlement is effected by pre-cooling the jar in a liquid nitrogen bath.'
rows.reasoning: RETSCH's own MM 400 page positively directs any application that needs sample cooling or heating to a different model (MM 500 control), and describes the MM 400 cryogenic mode as manual pre-cooling of the jar in an external LN2 bath (CryoKit = insulated containers, tongs, glasses). The MM 400 therefore has no controlled sample temperature range at all; the ice-cream recrystallization requirement (253.15-268.15 K) cannot be met. Numeric key marked not_available because the function does not exist on this machine, not because a number is missing.

rows.value_as_printed: Configured with stainless-steel jars; optical (in-situ Raman) access only with the separate transparent PMMA jar option
rows.quote: Transparent PMMA grinding jars are used for in-situ RAMAN spectroscopy but also enable applications with photochemical reactions.
rows.document_title: Laboratory Mixer Mill MM 400 - RETSCH (product page)
rows.location: Accessories section (cached research/v5/cache/c7591d067d40187a.txt line 459); CryoKit section line 447 ('stainless-steel grinding jar which is tightly screwed')
rows.reasoning: This configuration is explicitly the MM 400 with CryoKit and two 50 mL steel jars. RETSCH documents that optical access to the sample (in-situ Raman) comes from a distinct accessory, transparent PMMA jars, while the cryogenic mode uses tightly screwed stainless-steel jars. So optical access is an option not installed in this configuration (install optional_not_installed). Caveat: the PMMA option is for mechanochemistry and RETSCH ties LN2 pre-cooling to steel jars, so it would not rescue a cold optical experiment either.

rows.value_as_printed: No temperature control, hence no stability specification; sample warms during milling
rows.quote: For applications which require cooling or heating the sample, the Mixer Mill MM 500 control is the perfect choice.
rows.document_title: Laboratory Mixer Mill MM 400 - RETSCH (product page)
rows.location: Product description (cached research/v5/cache/c7591d067d40187a.txt line 305); also line 427: 'The sample is only moderately warmed in the process which can be reduced to a minimum by pre-cooling.'
rows.reasoning: Temperature stability presupposes regulated sample temperature. RETSCH states the MM 400 is not the model for cooling/heating the sample and that the sample warms during processing, mitigated only by pre-cooling. There is no temperature regulation function, so a 10 mK stability requirement has nothing to be checked against: not_available rather than an unknown number.

Vacuum freeze drying (sublimation under vacuum with a cold condenser) is not among its functions; the page mentions freeze drying only as a separate downstream step in an application example (line 535), performed outside the mill.
